heading: Apex & Baldy: The Okanagan's Smaller Ski Hills
title: Apex & Baldy Ski Hill Guide | Okanagan Roam
description: Apex and Baldy, two smaller Okanagan ski hills: night skiing, tubing, a forest skating loop, snowshoe trails, and where to eat after.
intro: Not every ski day needs a big resort. Above Penticton and Oliver, Apex and Baldy are smaller, family-sized hills where there's plenty to do off the runs as well: tubing, skating, snowshoeing and cross-country trails nearby.
Here's what's at each hill and where to eat once you're there. Each place shows its town.

items.name: Apex Mountain Resort
items.text: Penticton's home mountain, a short 30-minute drive from town, with 2,000 vertical feet and 1,112 skiable acres. Friday and Saturday nights, from 4 to 9 pm, the T-bar and Magic Carpet run under lights for night skiing, the tube park opens for night tubing and the skating loop stays open late.

items.name: Tim Hortons Tube Park – Apex
items.text: at the base area beside the beginner slopes, running on weekends and holidays through the season, with tubing under the lights on Friday and Saturday nights. Tickets are sold in two-hour blocks, and children need to be 42 inches tall to ride alone.

items.name: Adventure Skating Loop & Shinny Pond – Apex
items.text: a kilometre of Zamboni-smoothed ice looping through the forest, with the Shinny Pond beside it for pickup hockey. A new Skate Shack at the start of the loop sells skate passes and rents skates and helmets on weekends; it's weather-dependent natural ice.

sections.heading: Cross-country and the backcountry near Apex

items.name: Nickel Plate Nordic Centre
items.text: at 1,850 metres, 6.5 km past Apex Mountain Resort, with 45 km of groomed trails for classic and skate skiing, 22.5 km of marked snowshoe trails, and rentals, lessons and snowshoe tours. Dogs are welcome on the K-9 loop at any time.

items.name: Nickel Plate Provincial Park
items.text: a quiet, semi-wilderness park just past Apex Mountain Village, built around Nickel Plate Lake. In winter it turns to Nordic skiing, snowmobiling and ice fishing.

items.name: The Gunbarrel Saloon
items.text: a mountain lodge pub at Apex Mountain Resort with real pub fare and a friendly, chill vibe. Rated 4.4 stars.

items.name: Longshots Steak House
items.text: an upscale steakhouse in Apex Village from the team behind Shaughnessy's Cove and the Gunbarrel Saloon, with a rustic-cabin-meets-jazz-club atmosphere. Open Friday and Saturday, and reservations are recommended.

items.name: The Edge Bistro
items.text: a cozy grab-and-go bistro built around a ski-in ski-out takeaway window, with specialty coffees and sandwiches staff will kick up with extra flavour at no charge.

items.name: The Artisan's Den at Apex
items.text: a small coffee shop in the Apex Mountain Resort village, serving skiers and boarders their morning coffee before they hit the lifts. Rated 5 stars.

items.name: Pit Stop Cafeteria
items.text: a quick-bite cafeteria window in the heart of Apex Mountain Village for burgers, poutine and chicken strips between runs.

sections.heading: Baldy: the South Okanagan's ski hill

items.name: Baldy Mountain Resort
items.text: a small, friendly family hill with short lift lines. New for this winter is cat skiing from the top of the Eagle Chair to Baldy's upper terrain, and the Magic Carpet stays open until 7 pm on Friday and Saturday nights for tubing and beginner skiing under the lights.

items.name: Baldy Snowshoe Trails
items.text: about 13 kilometres of marked trail through the high forest around the day lodge. Go your own way with the resort's snowshoe map, rent snowshoes, or ask about a guided tour. Baldy is about 45 minutes from Oliver on a road that turns to gravel near the top, so bring winter tyres.

items.name: McKinney Nordic Ski Club – Snowshoe & Cross-Country Trails
items.text: a small, volunteer-run trail area a few minutes before the road reaches Baldy, with roughly five kilometres of marked snowshoe trail. Dogs and families are welcome and parking is free; the club's nine kilometres of cross-country ski trail are not being groomed.

items.name: Corduroy Cafe
items.text: the café and the upstairs Baldy Bar are the social hub for anyone staying at the resort, with trivia nights, live music and karaoke, and a kitchen that will swap bacon for a vegetarian option. Rated 4.4 stars.
